chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: that he was asked about a man passing along one of the roads of the Muslims, and his riding animal strikes a person with its leg. He said:

“He is not liable for what it strikes with its leg, but he is liable for what it strikes with its foreleg, because its leg is behind him if he is mounted. And if he is leading it, then by the permission of Allah he controls its foreleg, placing it wherever he wishes.”

He said: And he was asked about a Bactrian camel that became sexually frenzied and killed a man, then the slain man’s brother came and struck the male camel with a sword, crippling it. He said: “The owner of the Bactrian camel is liable for the blood-money, and he receives the price of his Bactrian camel.”
And regarding a man who startles another man so that he is injured, and his animal injures another man, he said: “He is liable for whatever resulted of anything.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood-money, the financial compensation due for unlawful killing
key_terms.بُخْتِيٍّ: a Bactrian camel, the animal involved in the case of killing a man
key_terms.بِرِجْلِهَا: with its leg, referring to a type of impact for which liability is negated here
key_terms.بِيَدِهَا: with its foreleg, referring to a type of impact for which liability is affirmed here
key_terms.دَابَّتُهُ: his riding animal or beast, the source of the accidental injury discussed in the ruling
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: liable or financially responsible for harm caused
key_terms.فَعَقَرَهُ: he hamstrung or crippled it, referring to the retaliatory striking of the camel

ai.seo_question: When is a person liable in Shia fiqh for injuries caused by his animal or by frightening someone?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning liability for injuries and death caused by animals and by a person’s actions in public pathways. It distinguishes between harm considered under a person’s control and harm beyond his direct control, and it affirms financial responsibility where causation and control are established.
